contentHtml:
Dubai is a land of golden opportunities. They city where business dreams turn into reality. That’s why it is called a global hub for entrepreneurs. If you’re a foreign investor and want to start a business in the Dubai Mainland, there’s one essential step you must take. You guessed that right! The first stepping stone is partnering with a local sponsor.

Mainland business sponsorship is regulated by the (DET) Dubai Department of Economy & Tourism in Dubai. It was formerly known as DED. Every sponsorship agreement, license issuance, and renewal must comply with Dubai rules. Moreover, office requirements and visa quotas should also be met.

We’ve written this guide to dive deep into every little detail. You’ll get insights on what a local sponsor means, why you need one, how to get a sponsor in Dubai, and what costs to expect. All in simple, clear language with Al Buraq!

Why Do You Need a Local Sponsor in Dubai?

About to set up a company in the Dubai Mainland? Under Dubai mainland business regulations, foreign investors must have a Dubai-approved Emirati sponsor who holds 51% of the company shares. This rule exists to support local participation in the economy.

But here’s the good news: you can still keep full control over your business operations and profits through the right legal agreements.

When Do You Need a Local Sponsor?

You’ll need a sponsor if your business falls under these categories:

  • Trading and retail businesses (buying/selling goods)
  • Manufacturing and industrial operations
  • Mainland services that aren’t part of free zones

You won’t need a sponsor if you’re setting up in a free zone where 100% foreign ownership is allowed. Don’t require a sponsor if you’re a consultant, doctor, or legal advisor. You only need a local service agent. Certain activities approved by the Dubai Department of Economy & Tourism (DET) allow full foreign ownership without a local sponsor.

Where to Find Legitimate Sponsors in Dubai

Get help from licensed business setup consultancies to access corporate sponsors. Connect with trusted business consultants like Al Buraq. They work only with verified individuals and sponsors. You can also find legit sponsors via Dubai Chamber initiatives and business programmes that connect investors with approved local partners. Trusted referrals from entrepreneurs, legal advisors, and networks also aid in finding reliable sponsors.

Dubai Mainland Areas, Where Sponsorship Is Required

Local sponsorship is required for mainland businesses. Those businesses operate in commercial areas across Dubai. This includes established districts such as:

  • Deira
  • Bur Dubai
  • Business Bay
  • Al Quoz, and
  • Jebel Ali (mainland).

These are the districts where businesses must comply with DET regulations for licensing, office space, and visas.

Dubai-Specific Documents You May Need

Certain local documents are required when setting up a mainland business in Dubai. These documents complete the sponsorship and licensing process. They maintain compliance with Dubai regulations and smooth approvals.

  • Dubai DET initial approval: Confirms your business activity and trade name
  • Ejari registration: Dubai’s official tenancy system is required for office and shop leases
  • Dubai Chamber registration: It is often needed for trading and commercial activities

Why Sponsorship Rules in Dubai Are Different from Other Emirates:

Dubai operates a more commercially focused sponsorship framework. It is designed to support high-value businesses and international investors. Sponsorship costs may be higher. However, the benefits often outweigh the investment.

Higher sponsor fees:

High fees reflect stronger legal protection, sponsors, and long-term stability. As compared to lower-cost markets

Faster approvals:

Approvals can be obtained fast through the Dubai Department of Economy & Tourism (DET). This reduces setup delays

Greater availability of sponsors:

Corporate sponsorships are offered for structured and secure partnerships

Access to Dubai-only business activities:

Companies can have access to Dubai business activities, not licensed elsewhere

Stronger banking and visa support:

Banking and visa support make compliance and scaling easier

Meet the Sponsor – Who They Are & What They Do

Types of Local Sponsorship in Dubai

Type Description Ownership Best For
Individual Sponsor A Dubai citizen (Emirati) acts as a sponsor 51% (on paper) Small to medium businesses
Corporate Sponsor A Dubai-owned company sponsors you 51% (contractually agreed) Larger businesses, long-term ventures
Local Service Agent A Dubai national handles admin work only 0% Doctors, engineers, and consultants

1. Individual Sponsor (Emirati Citizen)

This sponsor type is a Dubai national who legally owns 51% of your company on paper. You still control the business with a side agreement.

It is a common choice for general trading and retail businesses. Sponsorship for individuals often comes with a fixed yearly fee. Sponsors in Dubai usually stay out of daily operations

However, it is a must to sign a clear agreement to secure your rights. The sponsorship is better for small and medium-sized businesses

2. Corporate Sponsor (Dubai Company)

Instead of an individual, you partner with a Dubai-owned company. These sponsors offer more professional and secure arrangements. This sponsorship comes with clear contracts and legal protection. It reduces the risk of disputes or interference. Ideal for large corporations and industries.

This type of sponsorship has a more stable partnership. It has easier legal procedures and a predictable fee structure.

3. Local Service Agent (For Professionals Only)

If you’re setting up a consultancy, medical practice, or other professional service, you don’t need a full sponsor. You just need a local service agent. No ownership is given to the agent, and you have to pay a small yearly fee. The agent helps with licensing and government paperwork. It is best for consultants, doctors, engineers, and lawyers.

What to Look for in a Good Sponsor?

The right companion can make or break your business journey. Check the following things before you commit.

Do a Background Check

It is a compulsory step. Firstly, confirm if they’re a Dubai citizen or not. Check for legal disputes or financial issues. See if they’ve sponsored other businesses

Ask the Right Questions

  • Are they familiar with your industry?
  • Will they sign a side agreement to give you full control?
  • Do they prefer a fixed fee or profit sharing?
  • Can they provide business references?

Red Flags to Avoid

There are major red flags that don’t need to be ignored. If the other party refuses to sign a legal agreement, it means there’s something fishy. Check on deals that sound “too good to be true”. Sometimes, unclear terms or hidden fees are attached. You must keep an eye on them. Don’t blindly go for someone with no experience in business sponsorships.

What Will It Cost?

Sponsorship costs vary from case to case. It depends on the sponsor type, industry, and how the deal is structured.

Local Sponsor Cost Breakdown

Sponsorship Type Estimated Cost (AED/year) Fee Structure
Individual Sponsor 45,000 – 50,000 Fixed annual fee
Corporate Sponsor 30,000 – 100,000 Negotiated contract
Local Service Agent 8,000 – 10,000 Fixed fee, no ownership

What Affects Sponsorship Costs in Dubai?

In Dubai, sponsorship fees vary. It is based on various factors set by DET. You can budget accurately by understanding these cost drivers. This way, you can avoid surprises.

Business activity (DET categories):

Certain activities require higher compliance and attract higher sponsorship fees

Office location:

Mainland zones and premium areas often increase overall costs

Number of visas:

More employee visas mean higher administrative and sponsor involvement costs

Sponsor type:

Corporate sponsors usually cost more than individual sponsors but offer greater security

Banking & compliance support:

Businesses needing enhanced banking assistance or regulatory support may pay higher fees

These factors determine the final sponsorship cost for your mainland business in Dubai.

Fixed Fee vs. Profit Sharing: Which is Better?

Choosing the right payment model is important for peace of mind.

Fixed-Fee Sponsorship

In a fixed-fee sponsorship, you pay a set amount yearly. You have full control of profits and decisions. This model is most preferred by experts.

Profit-Sharing Sponsorship

It involves a sponsor who takes a percentage of profits. This can lead to disputes and complications. This model is less predictable and not ideal for startups

Legal Agreements: Protect Your Rights

Draft a legal agreement to protect your business. Do this when you find the right sponsor.

What to Include in the Contract:

The contract must include the confirmation that you keep 100% of the profits. The sponsor has no control over business operations. Add fixed fee terms and payment details. An exit clause in case you want to switch sponsors

Always consult a legal expert or business setup company to create a contract that follows Dubai laws and protects your interests.

Why Corporate Sponsorship is a Smart Choice

For many businesses, sponsors of corporate events offer more than compliance. They offer peace of mind as they are reliable and follow transparent legal procedures. Their assistance reduces the risk of personal disagreements. You can hire them as they are better suited for long-term or high-investment ventures.

How to Get a Sponsor in Dubai

You don’t have to search alone. Work with reputed business setup consultants who already have partnerships with trustworthy sponsors.

What a Consultant Can Do for You:

The right consultant will connect you with verified sponsors. On your behalf, they handle legal paperwork and licensing. They help you choose the right sponsorship model. Their presence assures that your business setup is fast and smooth.

Best Strategies Dubai Startups Use to Secure Trusted Sponsors in 2026

The following strategies can be used by Dubai startups to secure sponsors.

  • Work with licensed Dubai business setup consultants who have access to verified individual and corporate sponsors
  • Attend Dubai-based networking events and industry-specific meetups to build direct connections
  • Rely on referrals within established Dubai business circles for trustworthy introductions
  • Prioritise sponsors with proven experience in Dubai mainland businesses

Final Tips Before You Begin

  • Don’t rush into a sponsorship deal.
  • Ask for a contract before any payments.
  • Understand and protect your ownership rights.
  • Go for experience over low-cost offers.

Are You Ready to Launch Your Business in Dubai?

The right partnership with a sponsor is the first step. Helping you to build a successful business in Dubai. It is essential if you’re launching a retail store or a consultancy. The support of the professionals makes this process much easier. Get in touch with Al Buraq today. We can help you find the perfect sponsor. So that you can start your journey stress-free. Give us the chance to handle your complexities

Comparing Dubai with other Emirates? You can read our complete UAE business sponsorship guide. The guide has a full breakdown.

FAQs

Q: Can I start a business in Dubai without a local sponsor?

Yes, but only in free zones or if you’re offering professional services (then you’ll need a local service agent instead).

Q: Will I lose control of my company to the sponsor?

You can keep full control over finances and operations with proper agreements.

Q: Is corporate sponsorship safer than individual sponsorship?

Yes. Corporate sponsors offer more structured and secure partnerships.

Q: Can I change sponsors later?

Legal help is essential during the transition if your contract includes an exit clause.
